full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This appeal under section 410 of the Code of Criminal Procedure at the instance of Akkubbar Fakir is directed against the judgment and order dated 8-4-1997 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Khulna in Sessions Case No. 48 of 1995 arising out of Terokhada Police Station case No. 3 dated 13-2-1995 corresponding to GR Case No. 9 of 1995 under sections 302/34/114 of the Penal Code convicting the appellant Akkubbar Fakir under section 302 of the Penal Code and sentencing him thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Taka 5000. 

 3. Thereafter, the accused persons left the place of occurrence. Nurul Hoq Mollah, Hamid Sheikh, Jahangir Skeikh, Mokaddes Gazi and other brothers of the injured Akhter Gazi came to the house of the informant and saw the critical condition of the victim, while he was senseless. Thereafter, he was taken to the Khulna Sadar Hospital for treatment where he died at about 10-00 PM on the same date and other 3 injured persons including the informant also received treatment in the hospital. On the following day, FIR was lodged about the occurrence with Terokhada Police Station under sections 147/447/302/325/323/ 114 of the Penal Code. 

 4. Sub-Inspector Idris Mollah took up the investigation and during investigation he sent the dead body for post mortem examination, seized 'Ish', (the wooden part of the plough), lathies, blood-stained earth, etc and on completion of the investigation, submitted charge sheet No. 15 dated 28-4-1995 against the accused persons under sections 147/447/302/323/114 of the Penal Code. 

 5. The accused appellant along with 5 others were placed on trial on charge under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and the accused Keramat Ali has been separately charged under section 325 of the Penal Code in addition to the common charge of murder. The accused Hajera Khatun and Ranu Begum have also been charged under sections 302/114 of the Penal Code. All the accused persons stood at the trial and pleaded not guilty to the charge levelled against them. 

 After the close of the prosecution witnesses, the accused persons were examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to which they repeated their innocence and the defence did not adduce any evidence on their behalf. 

 10. At the time of hearing of the appeal, Mr Khan Tipu Sultan, the learned Advocate for the appellant, has placed before us the FIR and the other materials including the evidence on record and also the judgment of the learned Sessions Judge and submits that the learned Judge erred in law and facts in passing the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence which is based on mere surmises and conjectures and without any specific corroboration by the evidence of any reliable and independent witnesses. Hence, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence should be set aside and the appellant be acquitted of the charge levelled against him. 

 12. Mrs Umme Kulsum Begum, the learned Deputy Attorney-General with Mr AHM Obaidul Kabir, the learned Assistant Attorney-General for the State, submits that the appellant has been rightly convicted under section 302 of the Penal Code and sentenced thereunder to suffer imprisonment for life on proper appreciation of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record and no illegality has been committed by the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence. 

 13. In the face of the arguments advanced by the learned Advocates of the contending parties, we are now called upon to scrutinize the material evidence on record in order to come to a proper decision in this appeal. 

 The defence side gave suggestions to the effect that on the said date and time of occurrence, the informant parties along with the deceased Akhter Gazi attacked the house of the accused Akkubbar Fakir and, as such, a separate case was registered in Terokhoda Police Station. According to the defence suggestion, Akhter Gazi was injured by the PWs themselves at the time of alleged attack in the house of accused Akkubbar. Simultaneously, it has been suggested that the PWs attacked the house of accused Satter Fakir with arms at about 2-30 PM of the same day of occurrence. It appears from the evidence on record that counter-case was lodged by the accused persons against the PWs and others after about 4 days from the date, of occurrence. PW 1 also identified the alamats including plough 'Ish' and bamboo sticks by which the accused persons attacked. These alamats were marked as Exhibits I, II and III. 

 29. During cross-examination, the investigating officer disclosed that the accused Renu Begum, Akkubbar and Satter were found at the Terokhada Hospital under treatment of injuries and they were arrested from there on 13-2-1995. With reference to this fact, the accused side has tried to impress upon that the informant parties also attacked the accused persons and caused hurt. It appears that there is a counter-case, the trial of which has also been held simultaneously. It appears from the evidence on record that there was clash in between the parties causing injuries to several persons of both the parties. However, the same investigating officer appears to have conducted investigation in both the cases and submitted charge sheets. 

 To sum up the evidence on record, it appears that the deceased Akhter Gazi was attacked in front of the house of the accused Akkubbar at about 2-30 on the date of occurrence while he was returning home. There are several eye-witnesses in this case and of them PW 1 Abdur Rahman PW 3 Nurul Huq Mollah, PW 4 Abdul Hamid Sheikh, PW 6 Md Nurul Islam Gazi, PW 7 Aynuddin Gazi and PW 8 Jeheda Khatun have given testimony in one voice that they had seen the accused Akkubbar Fakir to strike blow on the head of the deceased, which not only caused profuse blooding but also caused several bone fractures. The brain and mentinges were also affected by the injury. The wooden part of the plough is a very heavy weapon and it is acceptable that blow by the said article could cause such fatal injury on the head which is the vital organ of a man. 

 30. There are evidence against the accused Hajera Khatun, who is said to have called her brothers namely, accused Akkubbar Fakir, Satter Fakir and Keramat Fakir, from the 'biel' and provoked them in the matter of committing the offence. It is not unnatural for a village woman to be quarrelsome in nature and, as such, she induced the accused persons to commit murder of Akhter Gazi. Because there is no evidence on record to show that the accused persons had common intention of committing murder and the murder was actually caused by provocation of Hajera Khatun. It is true that her provocation created hatred in the mind of accused Akkubbar Fakir which induced him to strike 'Ish' blow on the head of the deceased. 

 31. Having due regard to the aforesaid facts, circumstances and evidence on record, we have to hold that the accused Akkubbar Fakir struck serious blow on the head of the deceased which caused death of deceased Akhter Gazi. 

 34. On perusal of the record, we are of the view that Hajera and Abdus Satter induced the accused Akkubbar Fakir to strike a blow on the person of the deceased by a 'Ish' of the plough. In this respect, we may discuss some evidence on record here. 

 43. It appears from the evidence shown above that the accused Akkubbar Fakir inflicted 'Ish' blow on the head of the deceased Akhter Gazi being instigated by accused Hajera Khatun and being directed by his elder brother Satter Fakir and his act was done without knowledge and intention to cause death of the victim. The accused Akkubbar Fakir, being provocated by Hajera and Abdus Satter, thus had done the act. 

 44. It further appears from the evidence on record that "maramari" (free fight) took place between the parties following earlier occurrence between Hajera and Nurul Islam Gazi as a result of which Akhter Gazi died by the sudden 'Ish' blow of Akkubbar Fakir. Such death of the victim was without any premediation and such death was caused in a sudden fight between the parties and in consequence of such fight, accused Akkubbar Fakir inflicted Ish blow in the heat of passion and thus, such act clearly falls under section 304 part II of the Penal Code. 

 49. From the facts and circumstances of the case, evidence on record and discussion made above, we are of the view that the convict-appellant Akkubbar Fakir had no conspiracy, pre-plan or premediation for inflicting blow on the head of the victim. Being instigated by the accused Hajera and being directed by his elder brother accused Abdus Satter Fakir, he did so, without any intention to cause death of the victim. Therefore, intention to kill the victim appears to be lacking. Thus, the charge under section 302 of the Penal Code fails. The accused appellant is, therefore, liable for commission of the offence of homicide not amounting to murder punishable under section 304 part II of the Penal Code and we find him guilty under that section.
